subtopics.title: International Relations: Australia, Seychelles and the US
subtopics.summary: The Prime Minister's visit to Australia for the 3rd India-Australia Annual Leaders' Summit 2026 covered defence, nuclear supply, energy, cyber and sports cooperation. A State Visit to Seychelles, for its 50th National Day, produced digital payment, aid, health and legal agreements. The section also notes the 250th anniversary of US Independence celebrated on 4 July 2026.
facts: 3rd India-Australia Annual Leaders' Summit held in 2026
India-Australia bilateral trade reached about USD 50.2 billion in 2025
Renewed Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation replaced and expanded the 2009 Framework
Administrative arrangement under the 2014 Civil Nuclear Agreement enables regular supply of Australian uranium
Rooftop Solar Training Academy at PDEU Gandhinagar aims to train about 2000 women and youth
AustralianSuper announced an additional AUD 500 million for India's National Investment and Infrastructure Fund
Agreement between NPCI International Payments Limited and the Central Bank of Seychelles to facilitate UPI
India announced a US$175 million Special Economic Package and a Rupee-based Line of Credit worth 1,250 Crore for Seychelles

subtopics.title: Cybersecurity and Supercomputing
subtopics.summary: The Kudankulam nuclear plant faced an alleged ransomware data leak by World Leaks, which renewed concern about the security of critical infrastructure. India's response bodies include CERT-In, I4C, NCIIPC and the National Cyber Forensic Laboratory, while the UN Convention Against Cybercrime is the new global legal instrument. The section also records China's LineShine taking the top spot in the TOP500 supercomputer ranking.
facts: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu is India's largest nuclear power station
The alleged data leak was claimed by World Leaks, a ransomware group
Kudankulam reactors are Pressurised Water Reactors developed by NPCIL (India) and Rosatom (Russia)
CERT-In was established in 2004 in New Delhi as the national nodal agency for cybersecurity incidents
I4C was established in 2018 under the Ministry of Home Affairs
NCIIPC was set up in 2014 in New Delhi to protect Critical Information Infrastructure
National Cyber Forensic Laboratory in Hyderabad gives early-stage forensic help to State/UT Police
UN Convention Against Cybercrime is the first universal legal instrument; it enters into force 90 days after 40 States ratify
India is not a signatory to the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime (2001), which took effect in 2004
China's LineShine tops TOP500 at about 2.19 exaflops, located at the National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen

subtopics.title: Polity, Law and Minorities
subtopics.summary: A Joint Parliamentary Committee flagged centralisation and autonomy concerns in the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, which would create one apex regulator for higher education. The Delhi High Court laid down a structured Right to be Forgotten framework that balances privacy against open justice and freedom of expression. The National Commission for Minorities and the constitutional safeguards for minorities complete the section.
facts: Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill proposes an apex regulator to replace UGC, AICTE and NCTE
The proposed Commission works through three councils: Regulatory, Standards and Accreditation
Regulatory Council prescribes minimum standards for establishing HEIs; Standards Council frames learning outcomes
Bill excludes funding (grant allocation) from the Commission's mandate
Appeals are handled by the Central Government, not by an independent mechanism
Degrees may be awarded only by universities established under Central or State legislation
Delhi HC in Laksh Vir Singh Yadav vs Union of India (2026) laid down the Right to be Forgotten framework
Supreme Court in Puttaswamy (2017) recognised the Right to Privacy as a Fundamental Right under Article 21
NCM is a statutory body constituted on 17 May 1993; members serve a 3-year term; Jains were notified in 2014

subtopics.title: Economy and Statistics
subtopics.summary: The World Bank kept India in the Lower-Middle-Income group for FY2027, using Atlas GNI per capita thresholds that are updated every July. MoSPI's new monthly services production index measures real output of formal services against a base year, and in April 2026 most of its sub-sectors grew at double-digit rates. Inward FDI into India rose sharply in 2025, and Indian firms also raised their overseas investment.
facts: World Bank FY2027 retained India as a Lower-Middle-Income economy, a status held since 2009
Classifications use Atlas GNI per capita and are updated every July 1
Atlas method averages exchange rates over several years to reduce short-term volatility
FY2027 thresholds: Low up to US$1,185; Lower-Middle US$1,186-4,695; Upper-Middle US$4,696-14,575; High above US$14,575
India's GNI per capita in 2025 was USD 2760
Since 1987, the share of low-income economies fell from nearly 30% to 11%
New services index covers 19 formal sub-sectors, nearly 60% of the services economy; base year 2024-25
In April 2026, 14 of 19 service sub-sectors recorded double-digit growth
India's FDI inflows rose 44% to USD 38.9 billion in 2025, making India the 11th largest FDI recipient
India's overseas FDI rose 47% to USD 35.7 billion in 2025, making India the 18th largest source of global FDI

subtopics.title: History, Sports, Awards and Education
subtopics.summary: The section covers the American Revolution, from the 1765 Stamp Act to the 1783 Treaty of Paris, and the 4 July 1776 Declaration of Independence. It also covers the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, the 60th Jnanpith Award and the PGI 2.0 school education grading framework.
facts: Stamp Act 1765: Britain's first internal tax on American colonists, levied on printed paper
Boston Tea Party (1773): colonists dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor
Battles of Lexington and Concord (1775) marked the beginning of the American Revolutionary War
Declaration of Independence adopted on 4 July 1776, drafted mainly by Thomas Jefferson
Battle of Saratoga (1777) helped Benjamin Franklin secure a French military alliance
Treaty of Paris (1783) formally ended the Revolutionary War
23rd Commonwealth Games: Glasgow, 23 July to 2 August 2026, 74 nations and territories, 10 sports
India's contingent has 125 members including para-athletes; no teams in 3x3 Basketball or Netball
R. Vairamuthu selected for the 60th Jnanpith Award, the first Tamil poet to receive it
PGI 2.0 uses grade bands instead of rankings; Chandigarh was the first State/UT to enter Uttam-3 (766/1000)

quizzes.passage: India and Australia held the 3rd India-Australia Annual Leaders' Summit in 2026, during a visit by the Prime Minister of India to Australia. The two countries are guided by the India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement of 2022, and talks on a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement are still continuing. At the summit, the leaders adopted a renewed Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation and launched a Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap. Energy was another focus, and the leaders issued a joint statement on energy security. The leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to secure energy supply chains and to greater energy resilience amid global geopolitical uncertainties. They also operationalised an administrative arrangement under the 2014 Civil Nuclear Agreement. A Rooftop Solar Training Academy was inaugurated in Gandhinagar, and a new partnership on cyber security and critical technologies was launched. Sports cooperation moved ahead through a roadmap focused on high-performance sport and Para-sports, and Australia extended support to India's Gaganyaan Mission. IP Australia obtained access to India's Traditional Knowledge Digital Library to help prevent wrongful patent claims. In a separate State Visit, India's Prime Minister travelled to Seychelles for its 50th National Day, where agreements on digital payments, healthcare and legal cooperation were signed, and India announced a special economic package for the island nation.

quizzes.passage: India's partnerships with Australia and Seychelles produced a series of agreements in 2026. The 3rd India-Australia Annual Leaders' Summit covered defence, nuclear supply, energy, cyber and sports cooperation, and the two countries adopted a renewed Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation. The summit also recorded a joint statement on energy security and a roadmap to strengthen maritime domain awareness in the Indo-Pacific. A new partnership on cyber security, critical technologies and supply chains was launched, and three countries signed a trilateral agreement on frontier technologies. Australia also approved two Australian university campuses to be set up in Indian cities. Australia extended support to the Gaganyaan Mission, including a temporary space-tracking facility on the Cocos Islands. Sports cooperation was also taken forward through a roadmap covering high-performance sport and Para-sports. On a separate State Visit, India's Prime Minister travelled to Seychelles for its 50th National Day. A digital payments agreement was signed to introduce India's Unified Payments Interface in Seychelles, while a healthcare agreement with the Seychelles Ministry of Health aims to make medicines affordable. An institutional link was set up between an Indian foreign service institute and Seychelles' foreign ministry, and an extradition treaty was concluded. India also announced a special economic package for Seychelles and a rupee-based line of credit.

quizzes.passage: India's response to cyber threats is spread across several bodies, each with a separate role. In 2026, an alleged data leak from the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant appeared on the dark web, which renewed concern about the cyber security of critical infrastructure. The plant in Tamil Nadu operates pressurised water reactors, and the data was hosted by a cloud services provider that detected suspicious activity. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team acts as the national nodal agency for responding to cybersecurity incidents. A separate body was set up to protect critical information infrastructure from cyber threats. The National Cyber Forensic Laboratory provides early-stage forensic assistance to investigating officers of state and union territory police. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre provides a framework for law enforcement agencies to deal with cyber crimes in a coordinated manner. Globally, the United Nations has adopted a convention against cybercrime that aims to strengthen international cooperation. The convention's secretariat is based in Vienna. Meanwhile, the Budapest Convention is a Council of Europe treaty that addresses crimes committed through computer networks. The Cyber Commandos programme trains special wings in the states. A portal called CyTrain offers massive open online courses for capacity building. The incident drew fresh attention to how critical infrastructure is protected.

quizzes.passage: India's cyber security response is spread across several bodies. In 2026, an alleged data leak from the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu appeared on the dark web, raising fresh concern about critical infrastructure. The plant's reactors were designed through cooperation between an Indian public sector company and a Russian partner, and the data was hosted by a cloud services provider that detected suspicious activity. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team was set up in 2004 as the national nodal agency for cybersecurity incidents. Another body, set up in 2014, protects critical information infrastructure from cyber threats. A national forensic laboratory provides early-stage forensic assistance to police officers in states and union territories. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre gives law enforcement agencies a framework for dealing with cyber crimes in a coordinated way. The Cyber Commandos programme trains special wings in the states. Globally, the United Nations has adopted a convention against cybercrime, which aims to strengthen international cooperation and to prevent, investigate and prosecute cybercrimes. Its secretariat is based in Vienna, and the treaty will take effect once a set number of member states ratify it. Portals for training and data analytics also support the effort, including an online platform for cybercrime data across India.

quizzes.passage: The American Revolution began as political unrest and grew into open armed conflict. Tensions rose in the 1760s and 1770s as Britain imposed taxes on the colonists, and protests against taxation without representation spread through the colonies. The colonists' resistance became more organised, and boycotts and protests became common. Colonial militias showed that local forces could stand their ground against a professional army. In 1776 the colonies adopted a declaration that announced their separation from Great Britain and grounded the new nation in Enlightenment principles. The purpose of the war then shifted from seeking the rights of Englishmen to a struggle for the natural rights of all mankind. The conflict lasted several years before a peace was eventually agreed. The Revolution is remembered as the foundation of the United States, which marked the 250th anniversary of its independence on 4 July 2026. The Games are organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation and include sports such as athletics, swimming, track cycling and boxing. In Scotland, the Commonwealth Games were held in 2026, bringing together athletes from many nations and territories. Scotland has hosted the Games several times before, most recently in 2014. India's contingent for the Games included para-athletes. The mascot is inspired by Scotland's national animal.

quizzes.passage: The Commonwealth Games are organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation and are generally held once every four years. The 2026 edition takes place in Scotland, which has hosted the Games several times before. The first Games were held in 1930 under the name British Empire Games, and the idea of a Commonwealth-wide sporting competition is traced to an earlier 1911 event in London. The Games were officially renamed Commonwealth Games in 1978. India is participating in 2026 with a contingent of 125 members, including para-athletes. The Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary honour, was instituted by Bharatiya Jnanpith in 1961 and is presented annually to an Indian author for outstanding literary contribution. It covers the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, and posthumous awards are not given. English was added to the award's language coverage in 2013. The award carries a cash prize, a citation and a bronze statuette of Vagdevi. The Declaration was adopted on 4 July 1776 and formally announced the separation of the thirteen colonies from Great Britain. The Boston Tea Party in 1773 was a major act of colonial resistance to British taxation. Meanwhile, the American Revolution, which began with protests against British taxes in the 1760s, was a long struggle for independence.
